cases.sentence: Зверь, которого я видел, был похож на леопарда, но у него были ___ и львиная пасть .
cases.explain: «медвежьи лапы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The beast which I saw was like a leopard, and his feet were like those of a bear, and his mouth like the mouth of a lion. The dragon gave him his power, his throne, and great authority.

cases.explain: «другого зверя» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: I saw another beast coming up out of the earth. He had two horns like a lamb, and he spoke like a dragon.

cases.sentence: Он наделен всей властью ___ и действует от его имени.
cases.explain: «первого зверя» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: He exercises all the authority of the first beast in his presence. He makes the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast, whose fatal wound was healed.

cases.sentence: Он заставляет всех жителей земли поклониться ___, у которого зажила смертельная рана.
cases.explain: «первому зверю» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: He exercises all the authority of the first beast in his presence. He makes the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast, whose fatal wound was healed.

cases.sentence: Он заставляет всех жителей земли поклониться первому зверю, у которого зажила ___.
cases.explain: «смертельная рана» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: He exercises all the authority of the first beast in his presence. He makes the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast, whose fatal wound was healed.

cases.sentence: Этому ___ было дано вдохнуть жизнь в изображение зверя, чтобы оно смогло говорить и действовать так, чтобы был казнен всякий, кто не поклонится изображению зверя.
cases.explain: «второму зверю» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: It was given to him to give breath to it, to the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause as many as wouldn’t worship the image of the beast to be killed.
